suread: review R1 素读（只读 text/，未开 md）

facts.fact: 次日回工；车上 Gazzie 问她睡得如何
facts.anchor: Gazzie asked how I’d slept

facts.fact: Gazzie 给她一把应急钥匙环
facts.anchor: she handed me a ring of keys for emergencies

facts.fact: Gazzie 说想让她回文件房几天——因为脑震荡在恢复
facts.anchor: while she’d like me to return to filing for a few days—just while my concussion was healing

facts.fact: Gazzie 允许她休息时自由走动
facts.anchor: I could roam freely on breaks

facts.fact: Gazzie 午餐时露面，问起她的文件
facts.anchor: She even made an appearance at lunch, asking after my files

facts.fact: Harrison 对她扬眉
facts.anchor: Harrison raised his eyebrows at me

facts.fact: 她忍不住笑了
facts.anchor: I couldn’t suppress a smile

facts.fact: 连 Harrison 也看出她和 Gazzie 关系在改善
facts.anchor: Even he could tell that my relationship with her was improving

facts.fact: 她借机追问走失的鳄鱼
facts.anchor: I took the opportunity to ask about the loose alligator

facts.fact: Harrison 说 Joe 否认留过纸条
facts.anchor: Harrison said Joe denied leaving the note

facts.fact: Gazzie 既否认派她们去文件房，又承认收到过一张陌生笔迹的纸条把她叫到剥皮间
facts.anchor: Gazzie both denied ordering us to the filing room and admitted to receiving a note in unfamiliar handwriting

facts.fact: 两人都把纸条扔了
facts.anchor: Both of them had trashed their notes

facts.fact: 她的盘问至少确认一件事：有人专门针对 Gazzie
facts.anchor: at least my interrogation confirmed one thing: Someone had it out for Gazzie specifically

facts.fact: 还没查完，农场局势倒退
facts.anchor: the situation at the farm regressed

facts.fact: 周四午饭后几分钟，Harrison 报告有人毁掉了烘干房的皮
facts.anchor: Minutes after lunch on Thursday, Harrison reported that someone had shredded the skins in the drying room

facts.fact: 二十张皮全部被切成半英寸宽的条
facts.anchor: cutting all twenty into half-inch-wide strips

facts.fact: 皮条像派对流苏一样悬在天花板
facts.anchor: that dangled from the ceiling like party fringe

facts.fact: 到场时风扇还在吹，把碎片轻轻吹开
facts.anchor: The fans were still blowing when we arrived, gently parting the pieces

facts.fact: Gazzie 用指尖抚过一张碎皮
facts.anchor: Gazzie stroked a shredded skin with a fingertip

facts.fact: Harrison 抓另一张细看
facts.anchor: as Harrison grabbed another one, examining it closely

facts.fact: Harrison 说切口是剃刀或同样锋利的东西
facts.anchor: he claimed, been cut by a razor blade or something equally sharp

facts.fact: 她问损失多少钱
facts.anchor: When I asked how much the damage would cost the farm

facts.fact: Gazzie 把眼镜推进头发里
facts.anchor: Gazzie pushed her glasses into her hair

facts.fact: Gazzie 报价：五千左右
facts.anchor: Five thousand or so

facts.fact: Gazzie：不算糟，但本可能更糟
facts.anchor: Not great. But could’ve been worse.

facts.fact: 她问监控拍到什么
facts.anchor: When I asked if the cameras caught anything

facts.fact: 附近的摄像头又坏了
facts.anchor: the ones close by had cut out again

facts.fact: Gazzie 满不在乎，令她困惑
facts.anchor: which, confusingly, still didn’t seem to bother her

facts.fact: Harrison 说 Joe 有向客户送货的不在场证明
facts.anchor: he swore Joe had an alibi with a vendor, where he’d been delivering hides

facts.fact: 周五一早 Joe 把他们叫到农场
facts.anchor: Friday morning, Joe called us to the farm early

facts.fact: 太阳在谷仓后升起时他们查看地面
facts.anchor: While the sun rose behind the barns, we surveyed

facts.fact: 数百把牛排刀刀柄朝上插在繁殖塘围栏边
facts.anchor: hundreds of steak knives stuck in the ground, handle up, along the breeding pond fence

facts.fact: 围栏里几条鳄鱼的黄眼睛跟着他们移动
facts.anchor: several alligators’ yellow eyes tracked our steps

facts.fact: 几十条从水里探出来
facts.anchor: Dozens more peered out from the water

facts.fact: Gazzie 在她问出问题前跺步回办公室
facts.anchor: Gazzie stomped back inside the office before I could ask questions

facts.fact: Harrison 只是困惑地摇头
facts.anchor: Harrison just shook his head, bewildered

facts.fact: 她认同：这是警告？威胁？还是得意？
facts.anchor: was this a warning? A threat? Gloating?

facts.fact: 围栏另一边 Joe 蹲在草里逐把拔刀
facts.anchor: Joe crouched in the grass, pulling knives from the ground one by one

facts.fact: 他摆弄这些刀很自在、很顺手
facts.anchor: He handled them comfortably, smoothly.

facts.fact: 难怪——那些刀像他削橙子常用的那把
facts.anchor: they resembled the knife he constantly used to peel oranges

facts.fact: 听到脚步声他抬头
facts.anchor: At the sound of my footsteps, he looked up.

facts.fact: Joe 用夸张的客服腔问能帮什么
facts.anchor: What can I do for you?

facts.fact: 她咽下自尊，笑了
facts.anchor: Swallowing my pride, I smiled.

facts.fact: 她说只是有几个问题
facts.anchor: Just had a few questions.

facts.fact: Joe：没那个时间，同时拔出另一把刀
facts.anchor: No time for those

facts.fact: 她不理他，问有多少把刀
facts.anchor: Ignoring him, I asked

facts.fact: Joe：数到二百五就放弃了
facts.anchor: Lost count at two hundred fifty.

facts.fact: 叙述者注：他大约干到一半
facts.anchor: He was about halfway done.

facts.fact: 她惊讶地问他在外面待了多久
facts.anchor: How long have you been out here?

facts.fact: Joe：太久了
facts.anchor: Too long.

facts.fact: 五百把以上插进地里，一个人干要花几个小时
facts.anchor: Sticking five hundred or more knives into the ground would take several hours for someone working alone.

facts.fact: 如果是 Joe 放的，他早知道要在热天里拔出来
facts.anchor: If Joe had put them there, he must have known he’d be pulling them out in the heat.

facts.fact: 那需要某种决心、某种恨
facts.anchor: That took a certain amount of determination. Hatred.

facts.fact: 她自问：Gazzie 买下他家农场真让他这么介意？她的钱？她的性别？
facts.anchor: Did Gazzie’s takeover of his family farm really bother him that much? Her wealth? Her gender?

facts.fact: 她还有一件事要问
facts.anchor: One more thing

facts.fact: 她知道 Harrison 已经问过了，她想看 Joe 的反应
facts.anchor: I knew Harrison had already asked, but I wanted to see his reaction.

facts.fact: 她直接问：那天鳄鱼走失，是不是你给 Harrison 留条叫我们去文件房
facts.anchor: The day that alligator got loose. Did you leave Harrison a note

facts.fact: Joe 明显困惑，好像第一次听到这个问题
facts.anchor: He looked visibly confused, like he’d never heard the question before.

facts.fact: Joe：没有。现在我能干活了吗
facts.anchor: No. Now can I do my job?

facts.fact: 他站起来走到塘另一边，结束对话
facts.anchor: He stood and strode to the other side of the pond, ending our conversation.

facts.fact: 在储藏室她坐在地上，额头抵着一个文件箱
facts.anchor: I sat on the floor, resting my forehead on a filing box

facts.fact: 箱子比平时更酸臭
facts.anchor: which smelled even more sour than usual

facts.fact: 她的推断：放鳄鱼的人大概也割了皮、插了刀
facts.anchor: Whoever had put the live alligator in the skinning room had probably shredded the skins and planted the knives.

facts.fact: 同一人也造成了天花板漏水，一夜之间又全长出来
facts.anchor: That same person had also caused the ceiling leaks, which had all sprouted again overnight.

facts.fact: 也许连持续的藻华也是他搞的——大家都说反常，但她不太信
facts.anchor: They might have even finagled the constant algae blooms, which everyone agreed were abnormal, but I was less sold on that idea

facts.fact: 按网上的说法，人一夜之间造不出藻华
facts.anchor: according to the internet, people couldn’t cause them—not overnight.

facts.fact: 她把事件分成两组：鳄鱼与刀＝警告；皮、漏水、藻＝会升级的破坏行动
facts.anchor: Maybe the alligator and the knives were warnings, and the skins, leaks, and algae part of a sabotage campaign that promised to escalate.

facts.fact: 但她问：一个人怎么可能全部搞定
facts.anchor: But how could one person be behind all that?

facts.fact: Joe 是她的头号嫌疑，尽管否认且有不在场证明
facts.anchor: Joe, my prime suspect despite his denials and apparent alibis

facts.fact: Joe 一点线索都没给
facts.anchor: hadn’t come close to giving me a clue

facts.fact: 尽管 Gazzie 更有礼了，也没再向她交底
facts.anchor: despite Gazzie’s increased civility, she hadn’t confided in me further.

facts.fact: 要查下去就得扩大调查面
facts.anchor: I needed to broaden my investigation.

facts.fact: 她开始盘算农场其他员工
facts.anchor: I considered the farm’s other employees.

facts.fact: 除她/Gazzie/Harrison/Joe 外还有五个全职
facts.anchor: five other people worked at the farm full-time

facts.fact: Javier 与 Will 主要在外场
facts.anchor: Javier and Will primarily worked outside.

facts.fact: Seth 与 Benny-G 管肉
facts.anchor: Seth and Benny-G managed the meat.

facts.fact: 她在农场遇过他们，他们都不愿和老板的孙女闲聊
facts.anchor: they all seemed reluctant to chitchat with the owner’s granddaughter.

facts.fact: 她判断：最不依附这份生意的人也许愿意说——Nova
facts.anchor: But the person least attached to the business might be willing to share information. Nova.

facts.fact: 她抛下文件，学 Harrison 的做法在休息室冲咖啡
facts.anchor: Abandoning the files, I took a page from Harrison’s playbook and quickly brewed coffee in the break room

facts.fact: Nova 正埋头看杂志，抬头给出一个近乎微笑
facts.anchor: Nova, who was poring over a magazine, looked up with an almost-smile.

facts.fact: 小风扇吹她麂皮夹克的流苏，像碎鳄皮一样飘
facts.anchor: Her mini fan blew the fringe of her suede jacket, which fluttered like the shredded alligator skins.

facts.fact: Nova 以为来的是 Harrison；看清是她笑容就淡了
facts.anchor: She must have been expecting Harrison; her smile faded when our eyes met

facts.fact: 她直直盯着递过去的杯子
facts.anchor: she stared blankly at the cup I extended toward her

facts.fact: 她把杯子放在桌上一支点燃的大豆蜡烛旁
facts.anchor: I set it next to a lit soy candle on her desk.

facts.fact: Nova：我上班路上买星巴克（刻意翻页）
facts.anchor: I pick up Starbucks on the way here

facts.fact: Nova 不说话，她追加一句「这儿怎么样」
facts.anchor: When she didn’t say anything else, I added

facts.fact: Nova：Things?
facts.anchor: Things?

facts.fact: 她挥手示意空荡的前办公室：忙吗
facts.anchor: I waved my hand to indicate the empty front office.

facts.fact: Nova：不忙
facts.anchor: No.

facts.fact: 她问：摄像头今天又坏了？
facts.anchor: Cameras cut out again today?

facts.fact: Nova：要是有画面我早告诉 Gazzie 了
facts.anchor: I would’ve said something to Gazzie if we got any footage.

facts.fact: 她把 Nova 称为友善度的最终 boss
facts.anchor: Nova was like the final boss of friendliness

facts.fact: 对照：Laura Leigh 至少是真和善，即使觉得她怪
facts.anchor: at least Laura Leigh had been genuinely kind, even if she thought I was a weirdo.

facts.fact: 她把手背到身后忍住坐立不安，继续推进
facts.anchor: I held my arms behind my back to stop myself from fidgeting and pressed on.

facts.fact: Nova 冷淡地答：Sure
facts.anchor: she said coolly

facts.fact: 她直问：你觉得是谁干的
facts.anchor: Who do you think’s doing it?

facts.fact: Nova 在椅子上挪了挪
facts.anchor: She shifted in her chair.

facts.fact: Nova：我要是知道早就告诉 Gazzie 了
facts.anchor: If I knew, I would have told Gazzie.

facts.fact: 她想编个谎但编不出来，只能说真话
facts.anchor: I tried to spin a lie but came up empty. The truth would have to do.

facts.fact: 她说想帮 Gazzie 查出是谁
facts.anchor: I’m trying to help her figure out who did it.

facts.fact: Nova 投来一个出乎意料的理解眼神，像她第一天上办公室那次
facts.anchor: Nova shot me another surprisingly sympathetic look, like she had on my first day at the office, when she’d left me with the files.

facts.fact: 她猜想 Nova 不是主动刻薄，只是无聊
facts.anchor: Maybe she wasn’t being actively mean to me; maybe she was just bored.

facts.fact: 她说这没什么可怪她的
facts.anchor: I couldn’t fault her for that.

facts.fact: Nova：你觉得这会有差别吗
facts.anchor: You think that’ll make a difference?

facts.fact: 她心口一紧
facts.anchor: My heart squeezed.

facts.fact: 自问：赢得 Gazzie 真是无望的目标吗
facts.anchor: Was winning Gazzie over really such a hopeless goal?

facts.fact: Nova 端详她的脸片刻，叹气，把杂志面朝下扣在桌上
facts.anchor: After studying my face for a moment, Nova sighed and set her magazine face down on the desk.

facts.fact: Nova 第一猜想：PETA 的人，但她自己就否了——他们不在乎鳄鱼
facts.anchor: Obviously it could be PETA people, but I doubt it. They don’t give a shit about alligators.

facts.fact: Nova 提出两条：旧的甘蔗投资、她正在取得的磷酸矿
facts.anchor: there’s the old sugarcane investments, and the phosphate mine she’s acquiring.

facts.fact: Nova：环保行动者可能想破坏她
facts.anchor: Eco-activists might be trying to sabotage her or whatever.

facts.fact: 她意识到自己忘了 Gazzie 的其他生意
facts.anchor: I’d forgotten about Gazzie’s other business dealings.

facts.fact: 她问为什么
facts.anchor: Why?

facts.fact: Nova：两个行业都以伤环境出名
facts.anchor: Both of those industries are notoriously bad for the environment.

facts.fact: Nova 补充：尤其是径流，毒化当地水道
facts.anchor: Especially the runoff. Poisons local waterways.

facts.fact: 她不知道这些，但觉得自己本该猜到
facts.anchor: I hadn’t known that, though I supposed I should have guessed.

facts.fact: 她问：为什么专打农场而不打住宅？我们有径流进附近的湖吗
facts.anchor: Why would they target our farm specifically, though, and not our house?

facts.fact: Nova：Obviously（显然有），但周围农场都有，没听说别人有麻烦
facts.anchor: Obviously, but most farms around here do, and I haven’t heard anything about them having trouble.

facts.fact: Nova：只打我们说不通；不过可能是更私人的
facts.anchor: It could be more personal, though

facts.fact: Nova 深思着问：你听说过那两个卫星办公室吗
facts.anchor: Have you heard about the two satellite offices?

facts.fact: 她答：听 Aunt Virginia 讲过一点
facts.anchor: A little, from Aunt Virginia.

facts.fact: Nova：前主人们恨 Gazzie
facts.anchor: The former owners hate Gazzie.

facts.fact: Nova 压低声音做密谋状，说起八卦后更有精神
facts.anchor: She lowered her voice conspiratorially, slightly more energetic now she was gossiping.

facts.fact: Nova：那些生意手段据说很不客气
facts.anchor: The business deals were pretty hostile, apparently.

facts.fact: Nova：我一直说麻烦来自他们之一，但没人听
facts.anchor: I keep saying the trouble’s coming from one of them, but no one listens.

facts.fact: 她努力保持镇定——这是她第一条真正的线索
facts.anchor: I tried to stay calm, but this was my first real clue.

facts.fact: 也许 Joe 不是唯一嫌疑人
facts.anchor: Maybe Joe wasn’t my only suspect.

facts.fact: 她自嘲：Move over, Nancy Drew.
facts.anchor: Move over, Nancy Drew.

facts.fact: 其余问题都没有结果
facts.anchor: None of my other questions, however, were fruitful.

facts.fact: Nova 说不清前主人与 Gazzie 的过节细节，也说不出哪个更像凶手
facts.anchor: Nova claimed she didn’t know any specifics about Gazzie’s feud with the former owners, nor did she know which of the two was a more likely culprit.

facts.fact: 她明白再问不出进展，回文件房
facts.anchor: Realizing I wouldn’t make more headway, I headed back to the filing room.

facts.fact: Nova 在她身后叫她 Dart
facts.anchor: Dart?

facts.fact: 她探头到走廊拐角：Yeah?
facts.anchor: I poked my head around the hallway corner.

facts.fact: Nova：你手指上有东西
facts.anchor: You’ve got something on your fingers.

facts.fact: 她的指尖粉红配绿颜料
facts.anchor: my fingertips were pink and green with paint.

facts.fact: 自从鳄鱼事件后她一直在画那张张开嘶吼的嘴
facts.anchor: Since the incident with the loose alligator, I’d been trying to capture its mouth, open in a hiss

facts.fact: 画的是那条饱满厚实的舌头、黄白的牙
facts.anchor: the plump, thick tongue, the yellow-white teeth.

facts.fact: 之后遇到 Harrison，他对新理论有兴趣（或至少继续假装容忍她）
facts.anchor: he seemed interested in the new theory or, at least, was still pretending to tolerate me.

facts.fact: 他喝她带来养鳄棚当借口的水壶里的水
facts.anchor: He sipped from the water bottle I’d brought to the grow-out barns as an excuse to chat

facts.fact: 她不想让他以为她喜欢他
facts.anchor: I didn’t want him to think I liked him

facts.fact: 他望着田野，好像能看见她的主意在天边成形
facts.anchor: gazing across the field as though he could see my idea brewing in the distance.

facts.fact: Harrison：细节我不确定
facts.anchor: I’m not sure about the details

facts.fact: Harrison：Gazzie 在接手前把两位主人都得罪了
facts.anchor: I do know Gazzie pissed off both owners before taking over.

facts.fact: 她说 Nova 也是这么讲的
facts.anchor: That’s what Nova said, too.

facts.fact: Harrison：你跟 Nova 谈过？
facts.anchor: You talked to Nova?

facts.fact: Harrison：我以为她不在乎这儿发生什么
facts.anchor: I didn’t think she cared enough to notice what goes on here.

facts.fact: 她回：她注意的是你
facts.anchor: She notices you.

facts.fact: Harrison：我可没注意到（笑着）
facts.anchor: I haven’t noticed

facts.fact: 她由此断定他知道 Nova 的暗恋
facts.anchor: So he knew about her crush.

facts.fact: 她指责他故意无视她
facts.anchor: You’re ignoring her on purpose.

facts.fact: Harrison：别担心，我多分你注意力来补
facts.anchor: Don’t worry

facts.fact: Harrison：我额外关注你，作为补偿
facts.anchor: I pay extra attention to you to make up for it.

facts.fact: 她翻白眼却头重脚轻，像空气不够
facts.anchor: I rolled my eyes but felt light-headed, like I’d run out of air.

facts.fact: 自问：我们真的像朋友一样开玩笑了吗
facts.anchor: Were we really joking like friends?

facts.fact: 她说还有另一个想法
facts.anchor: I have another idea.

facts.fact: 她停下考虑切入方式
facts.anchor: Pausing, I considered my approach.

facts.fact: 她不确定 Harrison 有多喜欢 Joe；他们共事多年
facts.anchor: I wasn’t sure how much he liked Joe; they’d been working together for years

facts.fact: Harrison 似乎相信 Joe 的不在场证明，但两人除此之外并不亲近
facts.anchor: Harrison seemed to believe his alibis, but they didn’t appear close otherwise.

facts.fact: Harrison：Oh yeah?
facts.anchor: Oh yeah?

facts.fact: 她想：既然已经下水了——答案是 Joe
facts.anchor: Well, I was in it now.

facts.fact: Harrison 摇头否：没门
facts.anchor: Harrison shook his head.

facts.fact: Harrison：他很难搞，也确实不愿给 Gazzie 当雇员，但他诚实
facts.anchor: he’s honest.

facts.fact: Harrison：有意见会当面说
facts.anchor: If he has a problem, he says it to your face.

facts.fact: Harrison：真要伤她，他会放火烧了农场看着我们救
facts.anchor: he’d set the farm on fire and watch us try to put it out.

facts.fact: 她不完全信服；但她想让他明白她是认真的，他也许会回头告诉 Joe
facts.anchor: if I made it clear I was serious about my suspicions, he might report back to Joe.

facts.fact: 她不情愿地欣赏他替雇员说话这一点
facts.anchor: I reluctantly appreciated that he’d defended his employee

facts.fact: 他不会让随便谁来顶罪
facts.anchor: he wasn’t going to let just anyone take the fall.

facts.fact: 她说「Fine」，这个词在嘴里发酸
facts.anchor: the word sour in my mouth.

facts.fact: 向 Gazzie 提前主人这个想法没那么顺利
facts.anchor: Bringing up the former-owners idea to Gazzie didn’t go as well.

facts.fact: 她在屠宰房找到 Gazzie，门一开就急切地问是不是他们怀恨在心
facts.anchor: I found her in the slaughtering room and, when she opened the door, eagerly asked her if they might have it out for her.

facts.fact: Gazzie：他们没参与（喘着气）
facts.anchor: They’re not involved

facts.fact: 一只棒球棍悬在她手里
facts.anchor: A baseball bat hung from her hand.

facts.fact: 从半开的门里她看见一条不动的鳄鱼尾巴，赶紧移开眼
facts.anchor: Through the cracked door, I saw an unmoving alligator tail and averted my eyes.

facts.fact: 她的算盘：解决了破坏者，若 Gazzie 立她为继承人，也许就会认真对待她请求用击发枪
facts.anchor: If I solved the vandal problem and she named me heir, maybe she’d take my request to use a captive-bolt gun seriously.

facts.fact: 她问：你怎么知道
facts.anchor: How do you know?

facts.fact: Gazzie：为扩张生意，我们得给其他主人一点鼓励，让他们听话
facts.anchor: we had to give the other owners a little encouragement. So they’d fall in line.

facts.fact: 她缓慢重复「鼓励」并猜测：销售提成？降薪？
facts.anchor: Sales commissions. Pay cuts.

facts.fact: 她缓慢重复 Encouragement 一词
facts.anchor: Encouragement?

facts.fact: Gazzie：有的要多一些
facts.anchor: Some required more than others.

facts.fact: Gazzie 抿唇：这么说吧，有位主人庆幸自己买了火灾险
facts.anchor: Let’s just say one owner was happy he had fire insurance.

facts.fact: 她说不懂
facts.anchor: I don’t understand.

facts.fact: Gazzie 翻白眼后说明：她一个线人放火烧了他一间小棚，只为表明她是认真的，且不伤生意价值
facts.anchor: A contact of mine set one of his smaller sheds on fire.

facts.fact: Gazzie 强调：没有会伤害生意价值的东西
facts.anchor: Nothing that would harm the business’s value.

facts.fact: 她的结论：纵火。她犯了纵火
facts.anchor: Arson. She’d committed arson.

facts.fact: 不算全意外，但她想知道 Gazzie 是否在乎伤到人
facts.anchor: Not entirely surprising, but had she been at all concerned about hurting anyone?

facts.fact: 她的读法：Gazzie 看人像看鳄鱼，都只是达成目的的手段
facts.anchor: It was as though she considered people, like alligators, just a means to an end.

facts.fact: 自问：为了生意她还愿意伤谁
facts.anchor: Who else would she be willing to hurt for her business’s future?

facts.fact: 她把表情强行按住，说这就是动机
facts.anchor: Wrestling my expression into submission, I said

facts.fact: 她说的原话：听起来像动机
facts.anchor: Sounds like motive to me.

facts.fact: Gazzie：别联络他们任何一个，否则——（退回屋内）
facts.anchor: Do not contact either of them

facts.fact: 她没提对 Joe 的怀疑，也没照计划请求重新开始剥皮
facts.anchor: I didn’t bring up my suspicion of Joe or ask to start skinning again, like I’d planned.

facts.fact: 她 instead→改为：她一气之下走回储藏室（原文 Instead, I stomped back）
facts.anchor: Instead, I stomped back to the storage room.

facts.fact: 她本以为在 Gazzie 那边有进展，显然没有
facts.anchor: I’d thought I’d made progress with Gazzie, but apparently not.

facts.fact: 她怕按这速度永远查不出凶手也赢不到她
facts.anchor: At this rate, I’d never discover the culprit and win her over.

facts.fact: 她怕被卡在中间地带：Gazzie 只在怀旧时喂她几段家族史，其余时候忽略她
facts.anchor: I’d be stuck in a middle ground, where she fed me snippets of family history when she felt nostalgic but otherwise overlooked me.

facts.fact: 门口她打量面前的工作，试图忽略浓稠酸臭的空气
facts.anchor: I surveyed the work ahead, trying to ignore the thick, sour air.

facts.fact: 二十个箱子矗立在前
facts.anchor: Twenty boxes loomed before me.

facts.fact: 她撕开前一天开始的那个箱子，抽出一份文件
facts.anchor: I ripped open the one I’d started a day before, yanking out a file.

facts.fact: 纸软、潮、布满黑斑
facts.anchor: The paper was limp, damp, and covered in black spots.

facts.fact: 她立刻丢掉，在牛仔裤上擦手
facts.anchor: I dropped it immediately, wiping my hands on my jeans.

facts.fact: 她翻剩下的：文件全长了霉
facts.anchor: The files were covered in mold.

facts.fact: 霉味恶心：麝香般、古老、不祥
facts.anchor: They smelled vile—musky and ancient and sinister.

facts.fact: 她说这讲不通：那只箱子她一天前才在做
facts.anchor: I’d been working on that box only a day earlier

facts.fact: 文件当时不算好闻，但绝无长霉
facts.anchor: while the files hadn’t smelled pleasant, they certainly hadn’t been covered in mold.

facts.fact: 犹豫后她开下一个箱子：也霉了
facts.anchor: Those files were molded over, too.

facts.fact: 下一个、再下一个都一样，每一份文件都毁了
facts.anchor: Every single file, ruined.

facts.fact: 她脑中跳到养鳄棚：像藻一样，霉长得快得不可能
facts.anchor: Like the algae, the mold had grown impossibly fast.

facts.fact: 她判定：这不自然
facts.anchor: It wasn’t natural.

facts.fact: 她手心出汗、呼吸变浅
facts.anchor: My hands were slick with sweat, my breath shallow.

facts.fact: 她想象霉孢子从鼻孔飘进、堵住肺
facts.anchor: I imagined mold spores floating through my nostrils, clogging my lungs.

facts.fact: 极短的一瞬她想到 Ironheart，想到 Gazzie 坚持说它要永无止境地毁掉家族生意
facts.anchor: my mind flicked to Ironheart, to Gazzie’s insistence on his never-ending quest to destroy the family business.

facts.fact: 她说一秒也待不下去了
facts.anchor: I couldn’t spend another second inside.

facts.fact: 她摔上门，快步走向前办公室
facts.anchor: Slamming the door shut, I speed-walked to the front office.

facts.fact: 没人在视野里，但透过玻璃门能看见 Joe 的皮卡在停车场
facts.anchor: through the glass front door, I could see Joe’s pickup truck in the parking lot.

facts.fact: 她受不了撞见他在休息、手里那把刀盯着她看的那个画面
facts.anchor: I couldn’t bear the thought of catching him on a break, leering at me with that knife in hand.

facts.fact: 她转身走回侧廊
facts.anchor: Instead, I whirled around and headed down the side hallway again.

facts.fact: 用新钥匙环她溜进加工楼
facts.anchor: With my new set of keys, I slipped into the processing building.

facts.fact: 每个房间都在忙碌，全体员工接下来一周被要求在室内加快制皮以补损失
facts.anchor: all employees ordered inside for the next week to speed up skin production and recoup losses.

facts.fact: 空气里满是人汗与霉孢子
facts.anchor: The air felt thick with human sweat and mold spores.

facts.fact: 她呼吸越来越短，穿到后出口
facts.anchor: Breath shorter and shorter, I wound through the hallway until I came to the back entrance.

facts.fact: 门卡住了
facts.anchor: The door was stuck.

facts.fact: 她先轻推，随后绝望地用肩撞开
facts.anchor: I pushed it gently, then desperation took over and I rammed it with my shoulder.

facts.fact: 门给了，她踉跄出去，蝉在耳边不安地合鸣
facts.anchor: It gave, and I stumbled outside, where the cicadas thrummed in their unsettling chorus.

facts.fact: 傍晚前的太阳暂时晃瞎她
facts.anchor: The late-afternoon sun temporarily blinded me.

facts.fact: 然后她闻到死动物与血的气味
facts.anchor: Then I smelled it: the stench of dead animal and blood.

facts.fact: 这气味在农场不算罕见，但比平时更浓
facts.anchor: Not an uncommon odor at the farm, but it was stronger than usual

facts.fact: 她后悔下午吃了一整个古巴三明治
facts.anchor: I wished I hadn’t had an entire Cuban sandwich that afternoon.

facts.fact: 她用手捂住鼻子，眨眼直到眼前的景象固化
facts.anchor: Holding my hand over my nose, I blinked until the scene in front of me solidified.

facts.fact: 主楼与繁殖塘之间的草地上铺满动物尸骸
facts.anchor: Animal carcasses spread across the grass between the main building and the breeding pond.

facts.fact: 主要是鱼，也有鸭子、天鹅和一两只水獭
facts.anchor: Fish, mostly, but also ducks and swans and an otter or two.

facts.fact: 总数数百，也许五百
facts.anchor: Hundreds of carcasses in total. Five hundred, maybe.

facts.fact: 全部被切成两半
facts.anchor: All of them halved.

facts.fact: 更准确说：是被撕成两半，像被某种动物撕开
facts.anchor: More accurately, ripped in half. Like an animal had torn into them.

facts.fact: 她承认：若不是刚见过数千份一夜发霉的文件、见过藻持续爆发、见过幼年鳄鱼同步转身面向她、又夜夜在 Greer House 睡不好，她可能以为是人锯的、抛的
facts.anchor: I might have assumed a person—or, more accurately, a few people—had sawed up the carcasses. Dumped them there.

facts.fact: 她站在阳光下压着呕吐感，思绪失控
facts.anchor: my thoughts spun out of control.

facts.fact: 她想象残躯从地里一道看不见的裂缝滑出——这个世界与下一个世界之间的裂口
facts.anchor: I pictured the mangled bodies sliding out from some invisible crack in the ground, a rift between our world and the next.

facts.fact: 近处传来一声嘶气，轻得像雾
facts.anchor: A hiss sounded close by, soft as mist.

facts.fact: 她倒退，差点撞上已在身后关上的门
facts.anchor: Staggering backward, I nearly knocked into the door, which had closed behind me.

facts.fact: 她拉开门穿加工楼走廊冲进屠宰房
facts.anchor: burst into the slaughtering room

facts.fact: Gazzie 正挥棍打鳄鱼头，闷响一声
facts.anchor: as Gazzie swung her bat, hitting an alligator’s head with a dull thump.

facts.fact: 她太晕以至于没有怜悯，把看到的报告给 Gazzie
facts.anchor: Too dazed to feel pity, I reported what I’d seen.

facts.fact: Gazzie 一言不发跟她走
facts.anchor: She followed me without another word.

facts.fact: Harrison 在走廊找到她们，跟上来
facts.anchor: Harrison found us in the hallway and tagged along.

facts.fact: 外头 Gazzie 检视尸骸
facts.anchor: Outside, Gazzie surveyed the carcasses.

facts.fact: 她胸口因快走而起伏——也因别的东西
facts.anchor: Her chest heaved with the effort of power walking—and with something else, too.

facts.fact: 叙述者猜：Fear?
facts.anchor: Fear?

facts.fact: 她终于觉得破坏行为让 Gazzie 在意了
facts.anchor: Finally, the vandalism was bothering her.

facts.fact: 看到她受影响令人不安
facts.anchor: It was unnerving to see her affected.

facts.fact: Gazzie 轻声：这至少让我们退一天
facts.anchor: This is going to set us back a day at least

facts.fact: Gazzie：加上那些皮……
facts.anchor: Combined with the skins…

facts.fact: Gazzie 住口，嘴拧成皱眉
facts.anchor: She trailed off, mouth twisting into a frown.

facts.fact: 叙述者修正：她不是害怕，是沮丧
facts.anchor: She wasn’t afraid; she was frustrated.

facts.fact: Harrison 指出摄像头又停了，看着电网最近的镜头
facts.anchor: Cameras are out again

facts.fact: 那镜头的录像灯是灭的
facts.anchor: Its recording light was off.

facts.fact: 她说：他们能接触生意；她忽略不了 Joe
facts.anchor: I said, trying to ignore the humid air hanging on my shoulders like some malignant creature. I couldn’t forget about Joe.

facts.fact: 她问有人知道 Joe 在哪儿吗
facts.anchor: Does anyone know where Joe was?

facts.fact: Harrison：他剥了一下午皮，和 Javier 一起
facts.anchor: Skinning all afternoon

facts.fact: Harrison：我们出来时经过他们；晚点可以复核，但我不认为是这里的人
facts.anchor: We passed them on our way out. We can double-check later, but I don’t think it’s anyone here.

facts.fact: 她头晕：不是 Joe，还能是谁
facts.anchor: I felt dizzy. If it wasn’t Joe, who could it be?

facts.fact: Harrison：可能是知道无线摄像头多好黑的外部人
facts.anchor: It could be an outsider who knows how easy it is to hack wireless security camera systems

facts.fact: 她想到前主人，但反驳：这些事发生在几小时内，他们怎么知道今天所有员工都在室内
facts.anchor: But they did this over the course of a few hours

facts.fact: Harrison：他们运气好
facts.anchor: They got lucky

facts.fact: 她：他们还给你们俩留了条
facts.anchor: They left you and Gazzie those notes.

facts.fact: Harrison：有了摄像头权限和好时机，都可控
facts.anchor: Manageable, with security-camera access and great timing.

facts.fact: 她眯眼指出：前几天烘干房没有被撬，是用钥匙开的
facts.anchor: The skin drying room wasn’t broken into the other day. They used a key.

facts.fact: Harrison：谁都能撬锁
facts.anchor: Anybody can pick a lock.

facts.fact: 她：那好几把挂锁呢？
facts.anchor: And multiple padlocks?

facts.fact: Harrison：那种东西有工具
facts.anchor: There’s equipment for that kind of stuff.

facts.fact: 她不考虑就逐条被打回来
facts.anchor: He batted down each idea without even considering it.

facts.fact: 她看向 Gazzie 希望她在听，但 Gazzie 只是空茫地看着现场、揉太阳穴
facts.anchor: I glanced at Gazzie, hoping she was listening, but she was staring vacantly at the scene, rubbing her temples.

facts.fact: Harrison 踢了一条死鱼，棕色脏物从鱼腹流出
facts.anchor: Harrison kicked at a dead fish, brown gunk oozing out of its stomach.

facts.fact: 她提高声音问：为什么要做这些
facts.anchor: Why do this, though?

facts.fact: Harrison 复述她的 Why
facts.anchor: he repeated.

facts.fact: 她说：为什么要造这么多麻烦，不像工作量很大吗
facts.anchor: Why would someone cause this much trouble? Doesn’t it seem like a lot of work?

facts.fact: 她的判断：以 Gazzie 已经惩罚过其中一个的程度来看，她看不见那两位卫星农场前主人来做这件事
facts.anchor: I couldn’t see the former satellite-farm owners doing it, especially given how Gazzie had punished one of them already.

facts.fact: Harrison：我猜是动物维权者，他们什么疯狂事都干
facts.anchor: I bet it’s an animal activist. They do all kinds of crazy shit.

facts.fact: 她试着想象
facts.anchor: I tried to picture it.

facts.fact: 她的专业反驳：他们通常挺无聊，闯入设施不常见；真闯入也是拍虐待画面上传以左右舆论；更激进的会放动物，仅此而已
facts.anchor: they’ll take videos of animal abuse, like inhumane living conditions, then share them online to sway public opinion. More radical groups sometimes try to release animals, but that’s all.

facts.fact: Harrison：也许吧，但是——
facts.anchor: I guess, but—

facts.fact: 她：总不会为了抗议再杀更多动物吧（她说到兴头上）
facts.anchor: Would they really kill more animals as part of a protest?

facts.fact: 自陈：动物福利是她的本行
facts.anchor: Animal welfare was, after all, my wheelhouse.

facts.fact: 她的论点：我们不是普通农场；牛不跳；猪聪明可爱；鳄鱼……不
facts.anchor: We aren’t a normal farm. Cows skip. Pigs are smart and pretty cute. Alligators are…not.

facts.fact: 她说：维权者不为会咬人的丑动物辩护，品牌上划不来
facts.anchor: Activists don’t defend ugly animals that bite. It’s bad branding.

facts.fact: 她的收束：况且他们前几天不会把那头鳄鱼关进楼里——他们会把它放了
facts.anchor: they wouldn’t have released that alligator in the building the other day. They would have freed it.

facts.fact: Harrison：I don’t know, Dart, 也许他们觉得必须采取激烈行动
facts.anchor: maybe they felt like drastic action was necessary.

facts.fact: 她说：也许。但真不信 PETA 会锯动物来证明主张
facts.anchor: But I really don’t think PETA would saw up animals to prove a point.

facts.fact: 一阵风把腐肉味抬向他们，两人都退一步作呕
facts.anchor: A breeze lifted the smell of rotting flesh toward us, and Harrison and I took a step back, gagging.

facts.fact: 她的思路转了：凶手不留痕迹地制造混乱讲不通——除非真有非人的东西在动手，或至少在替某人助攻
facts.anchor: Not unless something inhuman really was at work—or, at the very least, assisting someone

facts.fact: 那种助攻就是让人忘记锁门的好运、保证没人恰好在错误的时刻转过拐角
facts.anchor: providing the kind of luck that made people forget to lock doors, that ensured no one turned a corner at the wrong moment.

facts.fact: Gazzie 阴沉地说：我们一直有麻烦，也永远会有
facts.anchor: We’ve always had trouble

facts.fact: Harrison 不自然地笑，Gazzie 懒得回应
facts.anchor: Harrison laughed uncomfortably, but Gazzie didn’t bother responding.

facts.fact: 她继续研究尸骸，大概正在想象一个模糊的怪物在农场里忙活
facts.anchor: She studied the carcasses, presumably imagining a nebulous monster puttering about the farm.

facts.fact: 末句：Ironheart 在驱散它的猎物
facts.anchor: Ironheart, scattering its prey.
